content.comment_body: Hello, I'm trying to send the digital input/output status from a [company_name] [product_name] to a DCS system using TCP/IP. I'm not sure how to achieve this and would appreciate any examples or advice. Has anyone done this before?
It's not clear what you mean by a DCS system. Could you provide more details?
The system is from Yokogawa. I need to send statuses such as: 0 bit if I/O is LOW, 1 bit if I/O is HIGH, and 2 bit if the wire isn't connected.
Does the DCS system support Ethernet TCP/IP using the S7 protocol, or does it accept Modbus TCP/IP? Please provide more detailed information.
As previously mentioned, it's Modbus TCP/IP.

Keep in mind that not all [product_name] models support Modbus TCP/IP. You need a specific version for that capability in the device selection. Do you have further details about the DCS system, such as the type designation or a reference to the Modbus addresses of the device?
Yes, I have the newest [product_name]. Currently, I only have an IP address and an Ethernet cable connected to my [product_name].
Can you clarify which device is the server and which is the client? Do you have the exact type of DCS system or any additional information?

Hello [user_name], you initiated this topic and are asking for help. [user_name] is trying to assist, but you're not providing basic system details. Is there an underlying issue? Are you using a Yokogawa Centum DCS? If so, do you have a DCSX3000 module (Modbus TCP & serial) setup as a communication processor? How is it configured? [url] Please address these questions, or our [product_name] expert may not be able to continue assisting you. Regards, [user_name]

The [company_name] [product_name] can't operate as a server for the DCS; it can only act as a client sending I/O status. Two possible methods to do this are using a network output block or an HTML server. I don't have direct experience, so I would appreciate guidance or an example from someone who has completed a similar integration.

My role only involves the [product_name] side—sending data. Everything concerning the Yokogawa integration has been handled separately by others. I am mainly looking for advice on converting digital I/O to bits so the other side can read it. I don't have trouble answering questions, but this is a simple project and doesn't require detailed Yokogawa information.

That is your perspective, not mine. To exchange data with a Modbus device, you must first clarify which device acts as the server and which as the client. After multiple posts, you have clarified this aspect. You also need to know which Modbus address the data should be sent to—there isn't a default for sending the status of input 1 to a Modbus device; the destination address must be determined.
Here's an image illustrating a potential solution. I cannot confirm if the Modbus address and Unit-ID are correct since no information has been provided.

Hello [user_name], you want Modbus TCP communication between the [product_name] and the Yokogawa DCS, with [product_name] as the client. Keep in mind, the client is the active participant that initiates the connection and data exchange. You need the server's IP address, relevant Modbus register addresses to read/write, and the Modbus function codes required. If your understanding about server/client roles is correct, providing this information is necessary for programming the data exchange. Alternatively, if [product_name] should act as a server for the Yokogawa client, the program must be adjusted, and you should supply your IP address and a list of local addresses for the data to be accessed. The Yokogawa programmer will then set up the connection and Modbus requests. See this forum discussion for reference: [url] Hope this helps, [user_name]
